newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: U.S. firm wins $140 mln Bangladesh power plant deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm wins $140 mln Bangladesh power plant deal.

text.p: Smith Cogeneration of the United States has won a $140 million deal to set up a 130-megawatt barge-mounted power plant in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong district, officials said on Tuesday.
Bangladesh's state-owned Power Development Board (PDB) and the U.S. firm signed a 15-year agreement on Sunday for power generation from the plant, which is expected to be completed early next year.
Officials said the firm would sell electricity to PDB initially at 2.23 taka (5.1 U.S. cents) per kilowatt hour using imported naptha as fuel for power generation.
However, they said generation costs could be reduced for the remaining 14 years when natural gas would be used as a fuel by the end of 1998.

A similar deal was signed on Friday with a consortium led by U.S. firm Enron International to build a 100-megawatt barge-mounted power plant near the capital Dhaka. PDB officials said another deal was expected soon for building another 100-megawatt plant.
Bangladesh faces a power crisis because the country generates only 1,850 megawatts compared with demand of 2,000 megawatts.
Officials said Bangladesh was seeking overseas investment to raise power generation to 3,100 megawatts by the year 2000 and 4,600 megawatts by 2005.
